source_text: Καὶ τὰς πολλὰς περὶ σώματος ἀνίει μερίμνας τεθαρσηκὼς ἐλπίσι ταῖς πρὸς θεόν, ὅτι σοί γε τὰ ἀναγκαῖα παρέξει διαρκῆ τροφήν τε τὴν εἰς ζωὴν καὶ κάλυμμα σώματος καὶ χειμερινοῦ ψύχους ἀλεξητήρια. τοῦ γὰρ δὴ σοῦ βασιλέως γῆ τε ἅπασα καὶ ὅσα ἐκφύεται· ὡς μέλη δὲ αὑτοῦ τῶν αὑτοῦ θεραπόντων ὑπερβαλλόντως περιέπει καθάπερ ἱερὰ καὶ ναοὺς αὑτοῦ. διὰ δὴ τοῦτο μηδὲ νόσους ὑπερβαλλούσας δέδιθι μηδὲ γήρως ἔφοδον χρόνῳ προσδοκωμένου· παύσεται γὰρ καὶ νόσος, ὅταν ὁλοψύχῳ προθέσει ποιῶμεν τὰς αὐτοῦ ἐντολάς.
thought_title: Release bodily cares and trust God's provision
orientation: Clement continues his direct address to the newly baptized, now urging release from excessive cares about the body through trust in God's provision.
pass_a_gloss: And release the many cares about the body, having taken courage in hopes toward God, that to you at least he will provide the necessary things, sufficient food for life and a covering for the body and defenses against winter cold. For of your king is all the earth and whatever grows from it; and as his own members he cares surpassingly for his own servants, just as his own sacred things and temples. Because of this, do not fear surpassing diseases nor the approach of old age expected in time; for disease also will cease, when with whole-souled purpose we do his commandments.

choices.why: The imperative means to let go or loosen; 'release' keeps the sense of letting go of cares rather than merely stopping them.
The perfect participle indicates a settled state of confidence resulting from prior action; 'having taken courage' preserves the perfect aspect.
διαρκής means lasting or sufficient for the need; 'sufficient' fits the context of God providing what is necessary.
The noun means things that ward off or protect against; 'defenses' captures the protective function against cold.
The adverb means exceedingly or beyond measure; 'surpassingly' preserves the intensive force.
ὁλόψυχος means with the entire soul; 'whole-souled' keeps the compound sense, and 'purpose' renders πρόθεσις as settled intention.

pass_b_english: Release your many cares about the body, having taken courage in your hopes toward God, because he will provide you with what is necessary: sufficient food for life, covering for your body, and protection against winter cold. For the whole earth and everything that grows from it belongs to your King, and he cares surpassingly for his servants as his own members, just as he cares for his sacred places and his temples. Therefore do not fear even overwhelming sicknesses, nor the approach of old age expected in time; for sickness too will cease when we keep his commandments with whole-souled purpose.

last_rejected.quote: having taken courage in your hopes toward God
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'having cast away many cares concerning the body, with hopes toward God'; no mention of taking courage.
last_rejected.fix: having cast away many cares concerning the body, with hopes toward God
last_rejected.ruling: τεθαρσηκὼς = 'having taken courage/been confident'; valid rendering, not an addition or mistranslation.

problems.why: Same Greek concept (God's people) rendered two ways; reader may miss connection.
Same concept rendered two ways in same section; reader may think them distinct.

fixed: members: The English already uses 'members' for μέλη, matching the glossary; no change needed.
temples: The English already uses 'temples' for ναούς, matching the glossary; no change needed.
defenses against winter cold: Changed to 'protection against winter cold' to avoid awkward abstraction while keeping the sense of ἀλεξητήρια.
